questions.question: In UPSC Environment: Ecology & Ecosystems, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Ecology (Haeckel). Ecosystem (Tansley). Ecocline : Gradual transition between two ecosystems. Ecotone : Sharp transition zone (e.g., Mangroves)."?

questions.question: In UPSC Environment: Ecology & Ecosystems, this exam clue belongs to which area: "The unique functional role of a species in its ecosystem (where it lives and what it does). No two species can have the same niche (Competitive Exclusion Principle)."?
questions.explanation: Ecological Niche: The unique functional role of a species in its ecosystem (where it lives and what it does). No two species can have the same niche (Competitive Exclusion Principle).

questions.question: In UPSC Environment: Ecology & Ecosystems, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Unidirectional flow. Lindeman's 10 percent law says only about one-tenth of energy passes from one trophic level to the next (Lindeman): Only 10% of energy is..."?
questions.explanation: Energy Flow: Unidirectional flow. Lindeman's 10 percent law says only about one-tenth of energy passes from one trophic level to the next (Lindeman): Only 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level. Energy decreases as we go up.

questions.question: In UPSC Environment: Ecology & Ecosystems, this exam clue belongs to which area: "1. Mutualism (+/+): Both benefit (Lichen). 2. Commensalism (+/0): One benefits, other unaffected (Barnacles on whale). 3. Parasitism (+/-): One benefits at others cost..."?
questions.explanation: Biotic Interactions: 1. Mutualism (+/+): Both benefit (Lichen). 2. Commensalism (+/0): One benefits, other unaffected (Barnacles on whale). 3. Parasitism (+/-): One benefits at others cost. 4. Amensalism (-/0): One harmed, other unaffected.

questions.question: In UPSC Environment: Ecology & Ecosystems, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Primary: On bare rock (Lichen as pioneer). Secondary : On already existing soil (after fire/flood). Seral stages lead to a Climax Community."?
questions.explanation: Ecological Succession: Primary: On bare rock (Lichen as pioneer). Secondary : On already existing soil (after fire/flood). Seral stages lead to a Climax Community.

lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Web of Life'. Ecology is the study of how organisms interact with their environment. We explore the components of an ecosystem, the flow of energy through 'Trophic Levels', and the various 'Biotic Interactions' (Mutualism, Parasitism). For UPSC, focus on 'Ecological Niche', 'Ecological Succession', and the '10% Law of Energy Transfer'. This is the foundation of environmental science.
